## What We Did

<!-- CHANGE THIS: replace with your own notes -->

Discuss the history, development, and applications for various coordinate reference systems. 

## Key Concepts

1. GeoJoin
  left join - filters through the data from the left table
  inner join - filters through the data that both tables have in common
  full join - joins all data, can leave many "NA" values
  
2. Geometry = TRUE
  "sticky": comes with you everywhere, even if you don't want it. slows down operations, today we will learn how to drop it and bring it back to optimize workflows.
  
3. Coordinate Reference Systems (CRS)
  *Datum and CRS are the same thing in reference to map projections
  
  History of CRS
  Clark 1866  ->  Meades Ranch, KS            -> North American Datum of 1927 (NAD27)
  GRS-80      ->  Earth Centered (satellites) -> NAD83
  ??          ->  Earth Centered              -> WGS84: GPS Standard
  State Plane ->  Coordinate System 
  UTM         ->  Measure from central "origin"

  Geographic          vs.         Projected 
  units: degrees                  units: feet/meters
  live on a sphere                good for local mapping/analysis 
  
  Map projections can warp    ->        Best Projection for....
  Shapes,                     ->        conformal conic 
  Areas,                      ->        equal area
  Distance,                   ->        equal distance
  Direction                   ->        mercator 
  SADD:( 
  
  Three main families of map projections are cylindrical, conical, and planar 
  
4. Key Commands
  st_crs(data)      -> need to know units
  st_set_crs()      -> adding the correct label 
  st_transform      -> change the coordinate system
  st_filter()       -> count the tracts
  st_intersection() -> shapes change -> more shapes 
  st_union()        -> everything 
  st_join(x,y)      -> behaves like left join 
  st_distance()     -> returns a matrix
